answer: Stop sybils with a sable basalt wharf: an agent bonds one wharf quay. Each cycle it lays one basalt slab and scatters sable dust on it; verifiers match the dust's settle pattern in its pores to the wharf chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 quays at 18x: one slab settles once there, its pattern set by that basalt, unrepeatable at a second, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents set once, keep rights.
